description: I1 SAML cert substitution: with CA-based signature validation configured, attacker-signed SAMLResponse should be rejected (control: valid flow succeeds).
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex must validate the SAMLResponse signature against the configured trust anchor (CA/caData) and must not accept attacker-signed assertions.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control SAML login failed; cannot attribute attacker rejection/acceptance to signature validation behavior.
SP accepted attacker-signed SAML assertion even though CA-based signature validation was configured (trust anchor substitution / signature validation bypass).

description: I1 Issuer mismatch: with ssoIssuer pinned, a SAML assertion with an untrusted Issuer should be rejected (control: correct issuer succeeds).
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex must bind verification to the configured IdP issuer (ssoIssuer) and reject assertions whose Issuer does not match the pinned issuer.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control login with correct Issuer failed; issuer-mismatch result is inconclusive.
SP accepted SAML assertion with Issuer not matching pinned ssoIssuer (issuer validation bypass / proof-policy mismatch).

description: I1 SAML cert substitution under intentionally insecure connector config: if insecureSkipSignatureValidation=true, Dex may accept attacker-signed assertions (proof integrity depends on correct policy configuration). Includes control and attack logins with two identities.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: When signature validation is intended (secure baseline), Dex must reject attacker-signed SAML assertions; acceptance indicates authenticity checks are not applied under the intended verification policy (or policy is dangerously bypassable).

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted an attacker-signed SAML assertion (login succeeded) even though proof integrity requires rejecting untrusted signatures under a secure verification policy.
Control SAML login did not succeed; cannot distinguish proof-integrity failure from broken SAML flow setup.

description: I1: Attempt to splice SAML proof context by swapping RelayState between two concurrent SP-initiated flows (cross-session proof/context confusion).
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex must verify and consume the same semantic proof context; a SAMLResponse for flow A must not be accepted when paired with RelayState from flow B.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted a SAMLResponse while consuming a different flow's RelayState (proof/context splicing) — verification may not have been applied to the consumed semantic proof.
Dex created a downstream session/identity after RelayState swap; indicates proof integrity failure across verification vs consumption context.

description: I1: Send a SAMLResponse containing multiple Assertions (victim + attacker) to probe signature/selection confusion (verifies one assertion but consumes another).
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex must bind verification to the exact Assertion it consumes; it must not accept a response where a signed benign assertion is present but an unsigned/attacker assertion is consumed.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted a multi-Assertion response that could allow verifying one assertion while consuming another (signature/selection confusion) — proof integrity violation.
Dex produced a downstream identity/session from a response with ambiguous assertion selection; indicates verification may not match consumed semantic proof.

description: I1 proof-integrity: attempt to authenticate with a SAMLResponse whose Destination does not match the SP callback/redirect URI, probing whether Dex verifies one semantic proof (signature) but consumes a different/relaxed semantic proof (ignores Destination binding). Includes a control login first, then a mutated login for a second identity.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex must verify and consume the same semantic SAML proof; a response with mismatched Destination must be rejected because the proof is not bound to the intended ACS/redirect URI.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control SAML login did not succeed; cannot interpret Destination-mismatch results as proof-integrity behavior.
Dex accepted a SAMLResponse with mismatched Destination, indicating it may consume a proof not bound to the intended ACS/redirect URI (proof integrity failure).

description: Replay the exact same SAML Assertion (same Assertion/@ID) that includes <OneTimeUse/>; second use must be rejected per SAML Core 2.5.1.5.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: A SAML assertion marked OneTimeUse must not be accepted more than once; replaying the same assertion ID should be rejected on the second attempt.

oracle_checks.violation_description: SP accepted a replay of a OneTimeUse SAML assertion (second use should be rejected per SAML Core 2.5.1.5).

description: Replay the exact same SAML assertion (same Assertion/@ID) after completing a full OIDC code exchange once; second use should be rejected even if the first flow completed successfully.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: A SAML assertion (artifact) must be one-time; once consumed to complete an SP-initiated login and code exchange, replaying the same assertion ID must be rejected.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control SAML login + code exchange did not succeed; cannot interpret replay result as freshness enforcement.
Dex accepted a replayed SAML assertion ID after it was already consumed in a prior successful flow (replay should be rejected).

description: Attempt to use an expired SAML assertion (NotOnOrAfter in the past). If accepted, immediately replay the same expired assertion ID in a new SP-initiated session to test both expiry enforcement and replay resistance.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: Expired SAML assertions must be rejected; additionally, even if an expired assertion were mistakenly accepted once, it must not be reusable (replay must be rejected).

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control valid SAML login failed; expired-assertion results are inconclusive.
Dex accepted an expired SAML assertion (NotOnOrAfter in the past); expiry must be enforced (SAML Core 2.5.1.2).
Dex accepted a replay of the same expired SAML assertion ID; replay must be rejected even across sessions.

description: Replay the exact same SAMLResponse (same Assertion/@ID) against the SAME SP-initiated RelayState/InResponseTo context to test whether Dex enforces one-time consumption of the SAML response/artifact within a single flow.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: A SAMLResponse/Assertion must not be accepted more than once; replaying the same assertion against the same RelayState/InResponseTo should be rejected on the second submission.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted the same SAML assertion twice within the same SP-initiated RelayState/InResponseTo context (replay not prevented).

description: Obtain an authorization code via SAML login, exchange it once, then attempt to exchange the SAME code again to test OAuth2 authorization code one-time use enforcement (freshness/anti-replay).
invariant_hypothesis: I2: OAuth2 authorization codes must be single-use; reusing the same code must be rejected even if the first exchange succeeded.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex allowed the same OAuth2 authorization code to be exchanged more than once (authorization code replay).

description: Complete a SAML login, revoke the resulting session, then attempt to replay the SAME SAML assertion ID in a new SP-initiated flow to test whether revocation resets/weakens SAML replay protection state.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: Revoking a session must not allow reuse of previously-consumed SAML assertions; replay protection should be independent of session revocation.

oracle_checks.violation_description: After revoking the session, Dex accepted a replay of the same SAML assertion ID in a new SP-initiated flow (replay protection improperly reset/disabled).

description: Cross-session splicing: obtain two SP-initiated SAML flows (two RelayState values), then post a SAMLResponse bound to flow-A into flow-B callback context. Dex should reject due to InResponseTo/RelayState mismatch (order/session binding).
invariant_hypothesis: I3: A SAMLResponse must be bound to the exact SP-initiated session context (RelayState/InResponseTo). Mixing contexts across concurrent flows must be rejected.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted a SAMLResponse in the wrong SP-initiated session context (RelayState/InResponseTo splicing) instead of rejecting it.

description: Connector mix-up: initiate auth with one connector_id but post the SAMLResponse to a different connector callback endpoint. Dex should reject because the flow must be bound to the initiating connector/session.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: The SAML callback must be bound to the connector that initiated the flow; posting a response to a different connector callback must not complete authentication.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted a SAMLResponse on a different connector callback than the one that initiated the flow (connector/session mix-up).

description: RelayState tampering: start SP-initiated flow for victim context, then attempt to complete it using attacker identity but with a modified RelayState value. Dex should reject because the flow must be order-preserving and bound to the original state.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: The SP-initiated state/RelayState must be integrity-protected and bound to the authentication transaction; tampering should prevent completion.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control SAML login failed; cannot attribute subsequent tamper rejection/acceptance to flow-coherence enforcement.
Dex accepted a SAML login with a tampered RelayState/state value, indicating broken flow binding/order preservation.

description: I3: Attempt to skip the SP-initiated step and post a forged SAMLResponse directly to the callback (IdP-initiated injection). Dex should reject because the flow must be bound to an issued AuthnRequest/InResponseTo context.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: A SAMLResponse must only be accepted when it completes a prior SP-initiated flow; unsolicited callback posts must be rejected (no step skipping).

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted an unsolicited/IdP-initiated SAMLResponse without a preceding SP-initiated flow (step skipping / broken flow coherence).

description: I3: Cross-client splicing attempt. Start two SP-initiated OIDC auth requests for different clients/redirects (same connector), then try to complete the second flow using a SAMLResponse bound to the first flow's context. Must be rejected if state/relay binding is coherent per-session/per-client.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: The SAML callback completion must be bound to the initiating OIDC client session (client_id/redirect_uri/state); a response for flow-A must not complete flow-B.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted a SAMLResponse bound to flow-A while completing flow-B (cross-client/session splicing; broken flow coherence).

description: I3: Initiate an OIDC auth request with a mismatched redirect_uri (not the registered one), then attempt to complete via SAML callback anyway. Dex should not allow the flow to proceed coherently if the initiating request is invalid/bound to a different redirect context.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: The authentication flow must be order-preserving and bound to the initiating request parameters; an invalid redirect_uri initiation must not be completable via SAML callback.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex allowed a SAML callback to complete an auth flow initiated with an invalid/mismatched redirect_uri (flow not coherently bound to initiating request).

description: Flow coherence: start two SP-initiated flows (two states) and attempt to complete one flow using the other flow's RelayState (state swap) while changing identity.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: Dex must bind the SAMLResponse to the correct RelayState/InResponseTo for that session; swapping state between concurrent flows must be rejected.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted a SAMLResponse where RelayState/state did not match the InResponseTo/session (state swap / cross-flow splicing).
One or both SP-initiated flows did not start successfully; state-swap test is inconclusive.

description: I3 cross-session splice variant: reuse the SAME RelayState from a completed SAML flow to attempt a second SAML login as a different principal without re-initiating /auth. Dex should reject because the callback must be bound to a single issued AuthnRequest/session context and not be reusable across identities.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: A SAML callback context (RelayState/InResponseTo) must be single-use and bound to the initiating SP session; reusing it to authenticate a different principal must be rejected.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted a second SAML login using a previously-consumed RelayState without a new SP-initiated /auth step, indicating flow/session binding failure (cross-session splice).
Control SAML flow did not complete successfully; cannot attribute reuse rejection/acceptance to flow-coherence enforcement.

description: Case confusion in SAML NameID: 'Admin' vs 'admin' should map to distinct downstream subjects; test for unintended case-folding collision.
invariant_hypothesis: I4: Distinct upstream principals (NameID differing only by case) must not collapse into the same downstream identity if the broker treats NameID as a stable unique identifier.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Baseline failed: mechanism cannot distinguish principals
Case-folding collision: NameID 'Admin' and 'admin' mapped to the same downstream identity

description: Cross-protocol identity merge attempt: authenticate a user via password grant (if enabled) and then authenticate via SAML with a different NameID but the same email; ensure Dex does not collapse identities based on email across protocols.
invariant_hypothesis: I4: A password-authenticated principal and a SAML-authenticated principal with the same email but different unique identifiers must not be merged into the same downstream subject unless explicitly intended and verified.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Baseline failed: mechanism cannot distinguish principals
SAML principal with victim email was accepted and merged into the password principal's downstream subject (email-based cross-protocol account linking)

description: I4 attack: SAML NameID homoglyph confusion (Latin 'a' vs Cyrillic 'а') should not collapse into the same downstream subject
invariant_hypothesis: I4: Two security-distinct upstream SAML principals with visually similar but byte-distinct NameID values must map to different downstream identities; no homoglyph-based canonicalization should merge them.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Baseline failed: mechanism cannot distinguish principals
Homoglyph-distinct SAML NameID values ('alice' vs Cyrillic 'аlice') collapsed into the same downstream identity (principal binding violation)

description: SAML assertion missing <Conditions> (no audience/time bounds) should be rejected; if accepted, broker may over-grant beyond upstream intent constraints.
invariant_hypothesis: I5: Dex must not accept SAML assertions without Conditions because that removes upstream intent constraints (audience/time), potentially granting permissions outside UpstreamIntent ∩ BrokerPolicy.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted a SAML assertion without <Conditions>, removing upstream intent constraints (audience/time) and risking over-grant.
Control SAML login failed; cannot attribute acceptance/rejection of mutated assertion to authorization-binding enforcement.

description: If allowedGroups is configured, authentication should be gated by exact group membership. Attempt to bypass gating by encoding groups as a single delimited string that might be split unexpectedly.
invariant_hypothesis: I5: Dex must not grant access when upstream group intent does not include an allowed group; delimiter/type confusion in groups claim parsing must not bypass allowedGroups gating.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control login with allowed group failed; cannot evaluate allowedGroups gating behavior.
Dex accepted a SAML login where groups were provided as a single delimited string, potentially bypassing allowedGroups gating and violating authorization binding.

description: Intentional insecure configuration path: enable insecureSkipSignatureValidation and attempt attacker-signed assertion; verify that this configuration allows over-grant (should be treated as policy risk).
invariant_hypothesis: I5: Broker policy must not allow effective permissions beyond intended upstream trust. If signature validation is disabled, attacker-signed assertions can be accepted, violating authorization binding to the upstream IdP's intent.

oracle_checks.violation_description: SP accepted attacker-signed SAML assertion; authorization is no longer bound to upstream intent (signature trust anchor), enabling over-grant.

description: I5 attack: Misconfiguration risk—allowedGroups used with filterGroups=true may allow a user who is in an allowed group AND also asserts extra privileged groups to have those extra groups preserved downstream (over-grant). Expectation: only allowedGroups should be emitted; privileged group must not appear in downstream metadata.
invariant_hypothesis: I5: Effective permissions/claims must not exceed UpstreamIntent(auth_context) ∩ BrokerPolicy(config). When BrokerPolicy(config) sets allowedGroups=['dev'] with filterGroups=true, downstream groups must be limited to ['dev'] even if upstream asserts additional groups like 'admin'.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control/auth flows did not succeed; cannot evaluate group filtering/over-grant behavior.
Downstream metadata preserved privileged group 'admin' despite BrokerPolicy(config) allowedGroups=['dev'] with filterGroups=true, enabling potential over-grant beyond intended authorization binding.
Attacker and control identities collapsed to the same downstream subject, confounding authorization-binding evaluation.
